newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch gold sale to boost government revenues.
newsitem.headline: Dutch gold sale to boost government revenues.

text.p: The Dutch government said on Monday the sale of 300 tonnes of gold from central bank reserves would boost government revenues by 250 million guilders a year.
The gold sale has raised $3.8 billion -- equivalent to 6.4 billion guilders. This money will remain part of the central bank's reserves but will now be held in interest-bearing assets.

In a letter to parliament, Finance Minister Gerrit Zalm said that at current exchange rates and interest rates the operation was expected to lead to an extra transfer of central bank profits to the government of some 250 million guilders per year.

The letter did not spell out whether the interest revenues from the gold sale would lead to a significant improvement in the EMU government deficit to GDP ratio. A Finance Ministry spokesman was not immediately available to clarify this point.

Government figures published with the 1997 budget in September showed that the deficit was expected to fall to 2.2 percent of GDP in 1997 from 2.6 percent in 1996 -- well within the EMU deficit goal of three percent.
Dutch public sector debt according to the EMU definition was expected to fall to 76.2 percent of GDP in 1997 from 78.8 percent in 1996 -- well above the EMU target of 60 percent.
